paragraphs.en: We use both words and body language to express our thoughts and opinions in our interactions with other people. We can learn a lot about what people are thinking by watching their body language. Words are important, but the way people stand, hold their arms, and move their hands can also give us information about their feelings.
paragraphs.cn: 在与他人的交往中，我们既用言语也用肢体语言来表达自己的思想和观点。通过观察人们的肢体语言，我们可以了解到他们许多内心的想法。言语固然重要，但人们站立、抱臂和移动双手的方式，也能为我们提供关于他们情绪的信息。

paragraphs.en: Just like spoken language, body language varies from culture to culture. The crucial thing is using body language in a way that is {appropriate} to the culture you are in.
paragraphs.cn: 正如口头语言一样，肢体语言也因文化而异。最关键的是，使用肢体语言的方式要符合你所处的文化。

paragraphs.en: For example, making eye contact — looking into someone's eyes — in some countries is a way to display interest. In other countries, by contrast, eye contact is not always approved of. For example, in many Middle Eastern countries, men and women are not socially permitted to make eye contact. In Japan, it may {demonstrate} respect to look down when talking to an older person.
paragraphs.cn: 例如，在一些国家，进行眼神交流——直视对方的眼睛——是表示感兴趣的一种方式。相反，在另一些国家，眼神交流并不总是被认可。比如，在许多中东国家，社交上不允许男女之间进行眼神交流。在日本，与年长者交谈时目光下垂，可能是在表示尊敬。

paragraphs.en: The {gesture} for "OK" has different meanings in different cultures. In Japan, someone who witnesses another person employing the {gesture} might think it means money. In France, a person encountering an {identical} {gesture} may {interpret} it as meaning zero. However, you should avoid making this {gesture} in Brazil and Germany, as it is not considered polite.
paragraphs.cn: "OK"的手势在不同文化中有不同含义。在日本，看到别人比这个手势的人可能会认为它表示金钱。在法国，看到同一手势的人可能把它理解为"零"。然而，在巴西和德国，你应该避免做这个手势，因为它被视为不礼貌。

paragraphs.en: Even the gestures we use for "yes" and "no" {differ} around the world. In many countries, shaking one's head means "no", and nodding means "yes". By comparison, in Bulgaria and southern Albania, the gestures have the opposite meaning.
paragraphs.cn: 即便是我们用来表示"是"和"否"的手势，世界各地也不尽相同。在许多国家，摇头表示"不"，点头表示"是"。相比之下，在保加利亚和阿尔巴尼亚南部，这两个手势的含义恰好相反。

paragraphs.en: There are also differences in how we touch each other, how close we stand to someone we are talking to, and how we act when we meet or part. In countries like France and Russia, people may kiss their friends on the {cheek} when they meet. Elsewhere, people {favour} shaking hands, bowing from the {waist}, or nodding the head when they meet someone else.
paragraphs.cn: 在身体接触的方式、与交谈对象站立的远近，以及见面与告别时的举动上，也存在差异。在法国、俄罗斯等国，朋友见面时可能会互相亲吻脸颊。在其他地方，人们与人见面时更喜欢握手、鞠躬或从腰部点头。

paragraphs.en: Some gestures seem to have the same meaning everywhere. Placing your hands together and resting them on the side of your head while closing your eyes means "sleep". A good way of saying "I am full" is moving your hand in circles over your stomach after a meal.
paragraphs.cn: 有些手势似乎在任何地方含义都相同。双手合十、放在头侧并闭上眼睛，表示"睡觉"。饭后用手在肚子上画圈，是表达"我吃饱了"的好方式。

paragraphs.en: Some body language has many different uses. Perhaps the best example is smiling. A smile can help us get through difficult situations and find friends in a world of strangers. A smile can break down barriers. We can use a smile to apologise, to greet someone, to ask for help, or to start a conversation. Experts suggest smiling at yourself in the mirror to make yourself feel happier and stronger. And if we are feeling down or lonely, there is nothing better than seeing the smiling face of a good friend.
paragraphs.cn: 某些肢体语言有着多种不同的用途。也许最好的例子就是微笑。微笑能帮我们度过困境，在陌生人的世界里找到朋友。微笑可以打破隔阂。我们可以用微笑来道歉、问候他人、寻求帮助或开启一段对话。专家建议对着镜子对自己微笑，让自己感到更快乐、更坚强。而当我们感到沮丧或孤独时，最美好的事情莫过于看到好朋友的笑脸。
